text:
ciara: Ran an nsys capture against the KV-prefetch stress test this morning. Timeline shows a large H2D memcpy on stream 7 that overlaps with inference kernels on stream 0/2. CPU side has 20-40ms wake gaps right after the memcpy finishes. pasted a tiny nsight excerpt below — not sure if it's host-copy blocking or our prefetch strategy. :thinking:

ciara: ```
Timestamp(ms)  Event                                      Stream  Duration(ms)
  12.34        memcpy H2D (layer-prefetch)               7       8.3
  15.90        kernel attention_forward                  0       2.1
  18.20        kernel qkv_matmul                         2       3.0
  20.60        memcpy H2D (pinnedpool blit)             7       1.2
  21.90        CPU sleep / sched wake                     -      25.4
```

ciara: Capture flags: `nsys profile --trace=cuda,osrt,syscalls -o /tmp/trace` + NVTX ranges around batch boundaries. Repro is microbatch=4, sequence=1024, kv-prefetch=true.

mike: can you paste the exact capture cmd (full args) and whether memcpy shows up as `cudaMemcpyAsync` vs host pinned copy? also how many concurrent streams? :eyes:

ciara: full cmd: `nsys profile --capture-range=nvtx --trace=cuda,osrt,syscalls --output=kv-prefetch-325 -f true --sample=none ./run_workload.sh`
ciara: nsight marks it as `H2D memcpy` and the API column shows `cudaMemcpyAsync` with stream 7. We create per-layer prefetch tasks that do `cudaMemcpyAsync` into pinned staging then enqueue an IPC-ish copy into the device pool.

anya: 20-40ms CPU wake gaps sound like host scheduling — maybe the thread that posts async copies is getting preempted after the final enqueue? did you check if the callback/submit is blocking on a small CPU syscall (e.g., futex) after the memcpy? try `strace -ttT -p <pid>` during the run to see syscalls latency.

raj: Also try toggling pinned vs pageable for that path. If the memcpy is large and pageable, driver will stage via host and cause more CPU involvement. microbenchmark suggestion: run a tight loop doing `cudaMemcpyAsync(dst, src, size, cudaMemcpyHostToDevice, stream)` with pinned vs pageable and nsight capture to compare durations.

ciara: good call — initial check: pinnedpool enabled. But we do a 2-step copy: host->pinned, then pinned->device in same submit. That pinned->device is the big H2D in stream 7. Could be we're copying whole KV for microbatch window (like 100MB) in one shot.

mike: if it's copying entire KV per microbatch, that's a red flag. For throughput you want chunked prefetch + overlap: small chunk copy + issue kernel that consumes prefix. Also look at kernel launch timestamps — if kernel starts only after full memcpy ends, we're serialized by design.

ciara: kernels on other streams do start while the memcpy is in-flight (see overlap), but CPU seems to go idle for a long time afterwards before next enqueue. suspect the host thread that launches subsequent microbatches is getting scheduled out waiting on something (maybe a CPU lock around the pinnedpool).

perf-bot: Alert: trace 3250000000 contains memcpy >5ms flagged in stream 7, potential host-induced latency. See /infra/traces/kv-prefetch-325 for raw capture. :robot_face:

anya: can you post a short grep of NVTX ranges showing prefetch boundaries? pattern like `PREFETCH: start` / `PREFETCH: end` helps align.

ciara: NVTX ranges snippet: ```
[PREFETCH_START] 12.30
  host_copy_layer 12.31..20.61
[PREFETCH_END] 20.62
[INFER_MICRO] 15.88..18.05
[INFER_MICRO] 18.10..21.80
```

ciara: note overlap: prefetch spans two micro-infers; we wanted that to be fine, but the late CPU wake suggests the submit for next prefetch is queued on a lock that only frees after pinnedpool blit completes.

raj: might be the pinnedpool free path uses a mutex and the host thread tries to allocate a new pinned buffer and blocks until one is returned. If all pinned buffers are in-use until the blit finishes, the allocation call could block and appear as a wake gap. replicate by instrumenting pinnedpool allocation latency (add NVTX around allocate/free).

mike: try both: 1) increase pinnedpool size to remove block, 2) change allocation path to `try_lock` and record a miss metric. If miss occurs, fallback to queueing async allocation or chunking prefetch.

ciara: I'll run two quick experiments: (A) double pinnedpool entries, (B) prefetch chunk size -> 16MB chunks with pipeline. Will capture nsys for both with `--capture-range=nvtx` to see per-NVTX timeline.

anya: also add `--trace=syscalls` to catch any futex/time nanosleep on host thread. and run `perf sched` to see if the host thread is being preempted by other high-priority work (cron/oom-killer unrelated stuff sometimes spikes in CI).

ciara: ran experiment A (bigger pool) — memcpy duration unchanged but CPU wake gaps reduced to ~2-4ms. So allocation blocking was a major contributor. experiment B (chunked) reduced peak memcpy and improved overall overlap, per quick nsight traces.

ciara: snippet from post-experiment trace (chunked): ```
Timestamp(ms)  Event                                      Stream  Duration(ms)
  12.40        memcpy H2D (chunk 1)                       7       2.1
  13.00        kernel attention_forward                  0       2.0
  14.20        memcpy H2D (chunk 2)                       7       2.2
  14.50        kernel qkv_matmul                         2       2.7
  15.00        host wake / enqueue next                   -      1.8
```

mike: nice. sounds like two orthogonal issues: pinnedpool allocation blocking + single large memcpy causing longer tail. chunking + pool size seems to fix both. we should add a regression test in runtime perf suite that exercises pinnedpool with saturating prefetch to catch future regressions.

ciara: Agreed. I'll open a PR with: (1) pinnedpool metrics (alloc latency histogram, misses), (2) default prefetch chunking to 16MB with autotune knob, (3) a perf test that runs the KV-prefetch microbenchmark under stress.

anya: for the PR include an `nsys` trace sample and a short perf dashboard screenshot link in the PR description so reviewers can eyeball the overlap. Also add a note on when to disable chunking for tiny models.

ciara: thanks — will draft the PR tonight and tag you all. tl;dr: nsight trace -> large H2D on stream 7 + pinnedpool allocation blocking caused post-copy CPU wake gaps; fixing pinnedpool sizing + chunked prefetch alleviates the issue. :thumbsup:

mike: awesome. once PR merges, let's schedule a 30min review on perf-regressions board to add the new test to CI. :calendar:

ciara: ping me if you want the raw `.nsys-rep` file, I can upload to the trace bucket.

raj: +1 — if you can also include a small reproducer script we can run locally, that'd speed validation.

ciara: will do. thanks all.
